fixes.explanation: Yes, every day. The LORD calls this pair of lambs a regular burnt offering "each day" (Numbers 28:3). Feast days get their own offerings later, but those are added on top. The daily pair is the steady rhythm underneath it all. Steady like my oven timer, which has never once asked for a day off.

Carmel is a good mountain name, but it isn't the one in the text. Verse 6 says this regular burnt offering was established at Mount Sinai. It's the only mountain the verse names. I guessed wrong on things way smaller than mountains back in my drawer days, so no shame here, friend.

Zion is a famous name, so I see why it jumped out. But verse 6 says this regular burnt offering was established at Mount Sinai. Zion shows up in a lot of places, friend, just not in this verse. Sinai is the mountain the text gives.

Doves are close to my heart, because Minty, one of my cookie cutter kids, is shaped like one. But verse 15 says one male goat is the sin offering here. The dove doesn't make this list. Sorry, Minty, not this time.

True. Verse 18 says, "On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work." So the feast opens with a sacred assembly and the regular work put down. A whole day off from regular work? I'd need a lie-down just thinking about a day away from my ovens.

Grain it is. Verse 26 says, "On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks…" So on the day of firstfruits, the offering is new grain. It comes with a sacred assembly and no regular work too.

Trumpets, friend. Verse 1 says, "This will be a day for you to sound the trumpets." It's a sacred assembly on the first day of the seventh month, and it comes with a sound you can hear. That's one day nobody could call quiet.

Seven days. Verse 12 says, "…you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days." That's the same length as the feast after Passover (Numbers 28:17). Then verse 35 adds a solemn assembly on the eighth day, so keep that one in mind.

False, and you read it right. Verse 35 says, "On the eighth day you are to hold a solemn assembly; you must not do any regular work." So after the seven days comes one more day with no regular work. The work can wait a little longer.

Guilt and ordination offerings aren't the pair this verse names. Verse 39 says "…in addition to your vow and freewill offerings…" Check the end of the verse and you'll find that pair. The ones you picked aren't listed there.
